ux.title: A stable data-driven agenda inside an annual conference site
ux.intro: The TCT agenda was not rebuilt as a new interaction each year. Its data request, grouping and session-display behavior were reused while each annual TCT site received its own visual treatment.

panels.title: Agenda data flow
panels.copy: An AngularJS Agenda service used $http and $q to request agenda data from app/data.php. Client-side processing grouped returned sessions by session_date and exposed the grouped result to the agenda controller.

panels.title: Session filtering + disclosure
panels.copy: The interface filtered the returned conference content to the correct session and presented session information through animated expandable/drop-down areas rather than separate static schedule pages.

panels.title: Annual presentation
panels.copy: The functional agenda stayed consistent across TCT years while the conference branding and front-end effects around it changed for each annual site.

16.note: Dallas Leipzig documents a reusable conference-interface component, not a one-off effect. ux.title: A reusable disclosure navigator for conference information
ux.intro: The Dallas Leipzig screen shows a stacked section navigator with a selected state and adjacent content panel. The same component pattern was reused on Fellows and other conference sites rather than being rebuilt independently for each event.

panels.title: Active section state
panels.copy: A vertical stack of section labels provided a clear current selection. The active row changed treatment and used a directional arrow to connect the selected label to the content panel.

panels.title: Expandable / changing content
panels.copy: The component supported changing or expanded conference content without sending the user to a separate page for every disclosure section.

panels.title: Reusable conference component
